title: Split compile_with and dsl::parse into phase-sized functions
description:
`compile_with` in `crates/apricity-score/src/compile.rs` runs from line 648 to about 1512: roughly 865 lines of validation, harmony fitting, voice assignment and event emission in one body. `dsl::parse` in `crates/apricity-score/src/dsl.rs` runs from 560 to about 1045. Ten `unwrap`/`expect` calls inside `compile_with` (for example `key.unwrap()` at 1297 and `.expect("resolved when there are no errors")` at 1307) rely on invariants established hundreds of lines earlier. Other oversized bodies: `s3.rs:381 handle` (~267 lines), `dsl.rs:1320 format` (~238), `compile.rs:190 route` (~229), `dsl.rs:262 effect_line` (~193), `cli/src/main.rs:115 main` (~135).

Done when: `compile_with` is a short driver over named phase functions (validate, resolve clips, fit harmony, assign voices, emit events), each with its own unit tests; `dsl::parse` is split per statement kind; no function in the score crate exceeds about 150 lines; every existing compile and DSL test still passes and the paired `.apr`/`.yaml` example equality test stays green.
